university: California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo

documents.title: Syllabus Statements: AI Core Values and Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single rule: "Please edit and adapt any of the following examples at your discretion" and offers three template tiers ("If AI use is prohibited", "restricted or limited", "permitted and encouraged"), so stance is delegates with tiers.
documents.summary: The teaching center offers core-value statements and three sets of sample syllabus statements (prohibited, restricted, permitted and encouraged) for instructors to copy or adapt. It sets no campus-wide stance and leaves the choice to each instructor, while tying all statements to the Academic Integrity Policy.

units.why: The page exists so faculty can state AI expectations up front; "help establish students' expectations about the course at the outset" is a communication rationale, typed P09 as the closest fit (expectation-setting in the syllabus) though it is a benefit statement rather than a mandate.
units.anchor: help establish students' expectations about the course at the outset
units.policy: Syllabus statements help faculty establish students' expectations about the course at the outset.

units.why: The page offers "examples of language that can be copied or revised"; faculty choose and adapt the wording, so the decision rests with each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: Please edit and adapt any of the following examples at your discretion.

units.why: The page says statements are "intended to support the development of transparent classroom policies and encourage thoughtful decisions to use, or not use AI", leaving use or non-use to the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: thoughtful decisions to use, or not use AI in teaching strategies and course design
units.policy: Resources support instructors in making thoughtful decisions to use, or not use, AI in teaching strategies and course design.

units.why: "any syllabi statements on AI usage should align with Cal Poly's policies on Academic Integrity" ties course statements to the university integrity framework; P56 (institution-level framework) fits better than P36 because it does not itself classify misuse.
units.anchor: any syllabi statements on AI usage should align with Cal Poly’s policies on Academic Integrity

units.why: The page points faculty to CSU AI Commons guidance as an official starting place; it is a pointer to a system framework, so P56.
units.anchor: Guidelines for Faculty Regarding AI in Instruction
units.policy: Faculty are pointed to the CSU's Guidelines for Faculty Regarding AI in Instruction as a good starting place.

units.why: "Use AI tools to support learning, not to circumvent academic responsibilities" is a core value limiting AI because it should serve learning; P41 (AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill) fits better than P19 as no specific output ban is stated.
units.anchor: Use AI tools to support learning, not to circumvent academic responsibilities.

units.why: "Distinguish your own original work by properly acknowledging all AI-generated content" tells students to acknowledge AI content; a disclosure duty (P24).
units.anchor: properly acknowledging all AI-generated content

units.why: "Be clear and honest about when and how AI tools have been used in your work" is a transparency value requiring disclosure of AI use (P24).
units.anchor: Be clear and honest about when and how AI tools have been used

units.why: "Disclose AI assistance in line with institutional guidelines" directly asks for disclosure; same type P24 as the prior unit but a separate sentence tying it to institutional guidelines.
units.anchor: Disclose AI assistance in line with institutional guidelines.

units.why: The example "This essay was drafted with the assistance of ChatGPT and edited for originality" models a disclosure statement; it names the tool, so P25 fits better than P24.
units.anchor: This essay was drafted with the assistance of ChatGPT and edited for originality.

units.why: "Always verify the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated information" is an accountability value requiring verification of AI output (P31).
units.anchor: Always verify the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated information

units.why: "you are ultimately responsible for the quality and originality of your submissions" says students own what they submit (P29).
units.anchor: you are ultimately responsible for the quality and originality of your submissions

units.why: "Treat AI-generated suggestions as starting points, not final answers" means students stay the primary thinker (P32).
units.anchor: Treat AI-generated suggestions as starting points, not final answers.

units.why: "AI tools may generate inaccurate or biased information" warns that output can be wrong or biased; P31 (verify, often wrong) fits rather than P53 because the point is student caution about output.
units.anchor: AI tools may generate inaccurate or biased information

units.why: "Apply your own analysis, reasoning, and creativity to refine AI outputs" keeps the student as the thinker over AI output (P32).
units.anchor: Apply your own analysis, reasoning, and creativity to refine AI outputs.

units.why: The gray-area question "Am I using AI as a tool to learn and create or as a shortcut to avoid effort?" is self-check guidance on the learning purpose of the work (P41).
units.anchor: Am I using AI as a tool to learn and create or as a shortcut

units.why: "Have I discussed how AI should and not be used ... with the instructor" prompts students in gray areas to talk to the instructor, which is the ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: discussed how AI should and not be used for learning and completing required assignments

units.why: "Would I be comfortable explaining how I used AI to my instructor or peers?" is a self-check of transparency and ability to explain use; closest is P30 (explain), though it concerns explaining use rather than code.
units.anchor: Would I be comfortable explaining how I used AI to my instructor or peers?

units.why: "Does this use align with my institution's academic integrity policies?" tells students to check their use against integrity rules; P56 as an institutional framework pointer.
units.anchor: Does this use align with my institution's academic integrity policies?

units.why: Example #1 for prohibited courses: "strictly prohibited in this course" bans generative AI across all work, so P01.
units.anchor: is strictly prohibited in this course

units.why: "All assignments, essays, and other submitted work must be your original, independent creation" requires submitted work to be the student's own (P29); P19 is not chosen because it names no AI-generation act here.
units.anchor: must be your original, independent creation

units.why: "submitting AI-generated work will be considered a violation of the Cal Poly Academic Integrity Policy ... treated as plagiarism" classifies misuse as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: submitting AI-generated work will be considered a violation of the Cal Poly Academic Integrity Policy

units.why: "may result in a failing grade for the assignment or the course" states concrete penalties (P37).
units.anchor: may result in a failing grade for the assignment or the course

units.why: Example #2 says "you may not use them in this course", a course-wide ban (P01).
units.anchor: you may not use them in this course

units.why: "you should not use generative AI to write, outline, revise, or polish any part of your assignments" bars AI from producing or polishing submitted work (P19; P21 covers checking work but the core is generation and revision of submitted text).
units.anchor: should not use generative AI to write, outline, revise, or polish any part

units.why: "When you submit your work, you're affirming that it's your own original creation" states students own their submissions (P29).
units.anchor: you're affirming that it's your own original creation

units.why: "If there is evidence that AI tools were used inappropriately, it will be addressed according to the university's academic integrity policies" routes misuse to integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: it will be addressed according to the university’s academic integrity policies

units.why: "I'm here to support your growth, and that starts with honest, authentic work" gives a learning/honesty rationale for the ban (P41).
units.anchor: that starts with honest, authentic work

units.why: Restricted Example #1: AI "may only be used for specific purposes and assignments ... as explicitly authorized by me" is the ban-unless-permitted default for the restricted tier; P04 (instructor sets) fits since the instructor authorises each use; P06 and P01 do not fit because it concerns listed authorised uses.
units.anchor: may only be used for specific purposes and assignments

units.why: "You may not, however, use these technologies for any other assignments or aspects of this course" bans AI outside authorised uses; a restricted-tier default (P06 fallback-like), chosen over P01 because it is conditional on authorisation.
units.anchor: You may not, however, use these technologies for any other assignments

units.why: "Any use of authorized AI-generated content must be documented and cited" requires disclosure for permitted use (P24).
units.anchor: must be documented and cited

units.why: "If you are unsure of how to use or cite AI in this course appropriately, please ask me" is the ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: If you are unsure of how to use or cite AI in this course appropriately

units.why: "Unauthorized use of AI in this course is a violation of the Cal Poly Academic Integrity policy and will be treated as plagiarism" classifies misuse as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of AI in this course is a violation of the Cal Poly Academic

units.why: "Violations may result in a failing grade for the assignment or the course" states a penalty (P37).
units.anchor: Violations may result in a failing grade for the assignment or the course.

units.why: Restricted Example #2: "You are welcome to use generative AI tools ... in this class as doing so aligns with the course objectives" for named assignments, an allowed-for-named-assignments rule (P04, per-assignment decision).
units.anchor: You are welcome to use generative AI tools
units.policy: Generative AI tools may be used in this class for the assignments that align with the course objectives (Creating Mission and Vision Statements, Creating a Sample Budget, and Creating Plans).

units.why: "You may not use generative AI for the remaining assignments" bans AI on non-named assignments (P04 per-assignment rule; the ban applies to everything else).
units.anchor: You may not use generative AI for the remaining assignments.

units.why: "You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query (for instance, that it does not violate intellectual property laws, or contain misinformation or unethical content)" assigns responsibility for submissions (P29).
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query

units.why: "Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited in order to stay within university policies" requires disclosure (P24).
units.anchor: must be properly documented and cited

units.why: "AI is not likely to generate a response that would be seen as quality work and should be modified and improved" says output needs human revision, i.e. critical evaluation of output (P31).
units.anchor: should be modified and improved

units.why: Permitted Example #1: "You are welcome to use generative AI tools ... and in some cases, you will be expected to do so" welcomes and sometimes requires AI, so P02.
units.anchor: in this class, and in some cases, you will be expected to do so

units.why: "AI usage should be documented and cited" requires disclosure under the permissive tier (P24).
units.anchor: AI usage should be documented and cited

units.why: "You are responsible for respecting intellectual property and ensuring that any information generated by AI is accurate and ethical" combines IP duty and verification; typed P52 because IP is the first named duty, accuracy being covered elsewhere under P31.
units.anchor: You are responsible for respecting intellectual property

units.why: Permitted Example #2: "you are welcome to use generative artificial intelligence (AI) models ... with correct acknowledgment" permits AI with acknowledgment (P02).
units.anchor: you are welcome to use generative artificial intelligence (AI) models

units.why: "you can ask the AI to cite itself in APA7 to help you" is a citation method for AI use (P25 cite the tool).
units.anchor: you can ask the AI to cite itself in APA7 to help you

units.why: "all large language models ... tend to locate incorrect facts ... perpetuate biases, create offensive products, and may violate copyright" warns about bias and harms (P53).
units.anchor: tend to locate incorrect facts and submit them as fact, make incorrect citations, perpetuate biases

units.why: "be sure that you consider ethical AI usage, data privacy and security, addressing potential biases" asks students to consider ethics and privacy; P50 is secondary, P53 chosen as ethics leads.
units.anchor: be sure that you consider ethical AI usage, data privacy and security

units.why: "you will be responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or unethical content you submit, regardless of its origin" is ownership of submissions (P29).
units.anchor: responsible for any inaccurate, biased, offensive, or unethical content you submit, regardless of its origin

units.why: "Any use of AI-generated content must be documented and cited" is a disclosure duty (P24); it is a distinct sentence in Example #2.
units.anchor: Any use of AI-generated content must be documented and cited

units.why: Addition #1: "AI should enhance learning, not substitute critical thinking and knowledge construction" keeps the student as the thinker (P32).
units.anchor: AI should enhance learning, not substitute critical thinking and knowledge construction.

units.why: Addition #2: "Use of AI is entirely voluntary and optional" says AI is not required, an equity/access safeguard (P51).
units.anchor: Use of AI is entirely voluntary and optional.

units.why: Addition #3: "you must accurately cite your AI use" and answer prompt questions asks for the prompt and output details, so P25.
units.anchor: you must accurately cite your AI use
units.policy: A student who uses an AI model must accurately cite the use and answer: What was your prompt? Was the AI model for your original output for your submission? Did you ask follow-up questions?

documents.title: Course Syllabi (academic policy)
documents.stance_why: The only AI content is the required syllabus item "Course policies governing the student use of generative artificial intelligence and other automated systems"; it mandates a statement but takes no position, so delegates.
documents.summary: The university syllabus policy requires every syllabus to include course policies on student use of generative AI and other automated systems, and requires discussing the syllabus on the first day. It sets no stance on AI use itself.

units.why: The university syllabus requirement lists "Course policies governing the student use of generative artificial intelligence" as minimum syllabus content, which is exactly an AI statement in every syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Course policies governing the student use of generative artificial intelligence and other
units.policy: Course syllabi shall at minimum include course policies governing the student use of generative artificial intelligence and other automated systems.

units.why: "Every instructor is required to make a course syllabus available ... at the first class meeting" is the rule for communicating syllabus content, including the AI policy, at course start; typed P09 since the AI policy rides on this syllabus duty.
units.anchor: required to make a course syllabus available to each student at the first class meeting

units.why: "Faculty are required to spend a portion of the first class meeting discussing the course syllabus" means expectations including AI policy are discussed at course start (P09).
units.anchor: required to spend a portion of the first class meeting discussing the course syllabus

units.why: "Some syllabus statements on course policies and use of generative artificial intelligence can be found at" the CTLT page points instructors to sample statements, supporting faculty in setting policy (P63).
units.anchor: Some syllabus statements on course policies and use of generative artificial intelligence

documents.title: Academic Senate Ad Hoc Committee on Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: It states no rule on AI use; it charges the committee to "formulate general guiding principles ... which should determine specific policies" by colleges, so the decision is handed to later bodies and colleges (delegates).
documents.summary: The page is the charge of an Academic Senate ad hoc committee to develop guiding principles, integrity principles, ethical-use guidelines and literacy resources for generative AI by the end of AY 2025-26. It is a charge, not a policy, and sets no stance.

units.why: The rationale says faculty set "academic standards and safeguards to ensure GAI supports rather than undermines Cal Poly's Learn by Doing mission", an institutional framing of purpose (P56).
units.anchor: set the academic standards and safeguards to ensure GAI supports rather than undermines

units.why: The committee will "develop a comprehensible, aspirational vision for GAI use at Cal Poly", an institution-wide framework in progress (P56).
units.anchor: develop a comprehensible, aspirational vision for GAI use at Cal Poly

units.why: Charge to "conduct a self-study of GAI use and attitudes" and publish findings collects evidence on AI use (P55).
units.anchor: Conduct a self-study of GAI use and attitudes at Cal Poly.

units.why: Charge to produce a brief "tracking trends in GAI use in higher education and industry" gathers evidence on AI use (P55).
units.anchor: tracking trends in GAI use in higher education and industry

units.why: Charge to "formulate general guiding principles concerning GAI use at Cal Poly" which colleges then turn into specific policy sets an institution-wide framework (P56).
units.anchor: Formulate general guiding principles concerning GAI use at Cal Poly

units.why: Charge to "develop resources for how to advance GAI literacy for both faculty and students" is AI literacy support; P63 covers faculty, and the charge names both, so P63 is chosen as the nearest type.
units.anchor: resources for how to advance GAI literacy for both faculty and students

units.why: Charge to support "GAI-literate faculty adopters and abstainers" provides faculty support and recognises that faculty may choose not to use AI (P63).
units.anchor: support GAI-literate faculty adopters and abstainers of the use of GAI in teaching

units.why: Charge to "formulate general principles of academic integrity with respect to GAI use" is an institution-level integrity framework (P56).
units.anchor: Formulate general principles of academic integrity with respect to GAI use

units.why: Charge to "provide guidelines to distinguish ethical and unethical uses of GAI by both faculty and students" is a framework on responsible use (P56).
units.anchor: Provide guidelines to distinguish ethical and unethical uses of GAI by both faculty and students.

units.why: The guidelines "would address issues such as privacy, data security, bias, accessibility, copyright/IP, disclosure, and responsible research/creative practice", listing responsible-use concerns planned for coverage (P56).
units.anchor: privacy, data security, bias, accessibility, copyright/IP, disclosure, and responsible research/creative practice

units.why: Charge to "review and make some recommendations on the use of specific GAI technologies at Cal Poly (e.g., ChatGPT.edu)" concerns vetted or licensed tools (P50).
units.anchor: Review and make some recommendations on the use of specific GAI technologies at Cal Poly

notes: Collect file found no school or computing-unit AI policy. Course layer deferred. The Senate ad hoc page is a committee charge listing planned work, coded as P55/P56/P63 for planning statements; CSSE faculty Foaad Khosmood sits on the committee (not coded as a policy). Several template examples contain bracketed placeholders.
